why_this_exists: This file records a REFUTATION, and it is the evidence behind the predicted_items telemetry field. planSynthesisHeadroom reserves a CONSTANT item allowance for what synthesis adds, so a natural hypothesis is that synthesis output scales with the member count and the reservation should be a per-member RATE. A revision of this package did exactly that and clamped the cohort to 7 members. These rows are why that was reverted: at 7 members the totals (21-41) OVERLAP the 10-member totals (28-39) completely, and the implied per-member rate went UP as the cohort shrank (2.80-3.90 at ten, 3.00-5.86 at seven). Total item count is largely INSENSITIVE to member count, so no clamp on members can bound it. The dominant term is whatever synthesis chooses to emit per group, which the plan does not control.
reading: Ten members: 28, 31, 32, 32, 34, 34, 39 (1 of 7 fit a 30-item ceiling). Seven members: 21, 27, 31, 37, 41 (2 of 5 fit). Cutting the cohort by 30% did not move the distribution. Bytes never bind on either population: the largest row is 141842 of 262144 (54%), so the item ceiling is the only binding axis and narrowing on bytes would narrow on the wrong quantity.
